positions.text: Sun, Zhou, and Guo provide independent evidence that several elements of Kaal's substrate-stage institution can be combined in an implemented validation system. Their decentralized peer-review model uses verified participants, a shared blockchain environment, token and reputation costs, public review evidence, and citable constructive reviews. They simulate the mechanism with KDD and ICLR data and implement a prototype on Ethereum and IPFS. This supports the feasibility of joining validation, standing, economic commitment, persistent evidence, and attribution in one institution. The qualification is substantial. The study concerns human scholars rather than autonomous agents. Its reputation is not capability-scoped REP. Its tokens are not Kaal's validator stake, and the model does not implement citation-weighted attribution, controlled propagation over a WDAG, or Kaal's exact staged deliberation. The source therefore qualifies the institutional pattern. It does not validate the complete substrate-stage architecture.

The model publishes citable review records but does not implement citation-weighted attribution or propagation over a WDAG.
Its review workflow is decentralized and may use multiple rounds, but it does not establish Kaal's exact staged deliberation architecture.
The relationship therefore qualifies only the feasibility of the bundled institutional pattern and does not validate the complete Kaal design.

sourceEvidencePassages.text: The reputation-based incentive provides guaranteed rewards to scholars who participate in peer review through permanent, publicly visible, and citable review reports that establish their expertise and contribution to the field.

locator.section: Materials and methods > Incentive mechanism for decentralized peer review

sourceEvidencePassages.text: A constructive review will be attached to the reviewed paper as a supporting document; therefore, it shares the credibility of the paper. The work will be awarded by the reputation sharing and the reviewer should contribute tokens to the paper’s account to pay for the participation.

locator.section: Materials and methods > Critical and constructive reviews

sourceEvidencePassages.text: Shared computing environment: a publicly verifiable computer (e.g., a trusted execution environment or a blockchain) that operates on a distributed network, allowing participants to execute and verify the peer-review logic, including token management and incentive mechanisms.

Reviewers could either earn tokens as rewards for efforts or earn reputation for participating in the publication process. Since a review is more than just an assessment of a paper—it is also publishable and citable—reviewers' scientific contributions to the papers will be recognized by the community.

locator.section: Discussion > Core findings and model effectiveness

sourceEvidencePassages.text: While the dual-incentive mechanism encourages higher review coverage, our model addresses the challenge of review quality through multiple mechanisms: (1) verified academic identities linked to all reviews create accountability; (2) the dual-rewarding system discourages low-quality reviews through both token and reputation costs; and (3) permanent blockchain records enable detection of undeclared conflicts or coordinated negative reviews.
